If an entity becomes aware of errors made under its previous financial reporting framework, the reconciliations required by paragraphs 35.13(b) and (c) shall, to the extent practicable, distinguish the correction of those errors from changes in accounting policies.
Disclose the fact that no financial statements were presented for previous periods, in the entity's first financial statements that conform to FRS 102.
A retirement benefit plan shall disclose information that enables users of its financial statements to evaluate the significance of financial instruments for its financial position and performance.

The notes to the accounts must state the average number of persons employed by the company in the financial year, determined as the monthly average (Companies Act 2006 s411). Medium and large companies must also analyse it by category of employee.
Present a statement of cash flows that classifies cash flows for the reporting period under operating activities, investing activities and financing activities.

A complete set of financial statements shall include all of the following: a statement of financial position (balance sheet); an income statement or a statement of comprehensive income; a statement of changes in equity; a statement of cash flows; and notes comprising a summary of significant accounting policies and other explanatory information.
Disclose the accounting policies employed in the preparation of the financial statements
Disclose any changes in accounting policies and the effects of such changes
Disclose any changes in accounting policies and the effects of such changes
Do not offset assets and liabilities, or income and expenses, unless required or permitted by an FRS.
Present separately each material class of similar items; also present separately items of a dissimilar nature or function unless they are immaterial.
Include an explicit and unreserved statement in the notes that the financial statements comply with FRS 102.

Where the reporting period end date has changed and the annual financial statements cover a period longer or shorter than one year, disclose the required information as specified in paragraph 3.10 (the reason for the longer or shorter period and the fact that comparative amounts are not entirely comparable).

When the reporting period end has changed and the financial statements are presented for a period longer or shorter than one year, disclose: (a) the period covered by the financial statements, and (b) the reason for the longer or shorter period.
Present comparative information in respect of the preceding period for all amounts presented in the current period's financial statements, except where this FRS permits or requires otherwise.
Present, as a minimum, two of each required financial statement and the related notes, because comparative amounts for the previous period are required for all amounts presented (per paragraph 3.14).
Present a statement of financial position (balance sheet) in accordance with the applicable balance sheet format requirements

An entity choosing to apply paragraph 1A(1) of Schedule 1 to the Regulations shall also disclose, either in the statement of financial position or in the notes, the sub-classifications of the line items presented (as enumerated in the sub-paragraphs of paragraph 4.2B).

Present total comprehensive income for the period either in a single statement of comprehensive income or in two separate statements (a statement of profit or loss and a separate statement of comprehensive income)

Present items to be included in a profit and loss account within the statement of comprehensive income in accordance with one of the format requirements set out in FRS 102 paragraph 5.5 (sub-paragraphs (a)–(c)).

When applying paragraph 1A(2) of Schedule 1 to the Regulations to adapt a profit and loss account format, include as a minimum in the statement of comprehensive income line items presenting the specific amounts enumerated in FRS 102 paragraph 5.5B for the period.

Under the two-statement approach, present in a separate income statement all items required to be included in a profit and loss account in accordance with the applicable profit and loss account presentation requirements (as set out in the requirements following paragraph 5.7).

When adapting a profit and loss account format under paragraph 1A(2) of Schedule 1, include in the income statement, as a minimum, line items presenting the amounts in paragraphs 5.5B(a) to 5.5B(g), with profit or loss as the last line.

Where the entity adapts a profit and loss account format under paragraph 1A(2) of Schedule 1 and presents a statement of comprehensive income, that statement shall begin with profit or loss as its first line and shall display, as a minimum, line items presenting the amounts in paragraphs 5.5B(h) to 5.5B(j) and 5.6(b) for the period, with total comprehensive income as the last line.

When adapting a profit and loss account format under paragraph 1A(2) of Schedule 1 to the Regulations, ensure the income statement includes, as a minimum, line items presenting the amounts in paragraphs 5.5B(a) to 5.5B(g), with profit or loss as the last line.

When adapting a profit and loss account format under paragraph 1A(2) of Schedule 1 to the Regulations, ensure the statement of comprehensive income begins with profit or loss as its first line and displays, as a minimum, line items presenting the amounts in paragraphs 5.5B(h) to 5.5B(j) and paragraph 5.6(b) for the period, with total comprehensive income as the last line.
Present turnover as a minimum line item on the face of the income statement (or statement of comprehensive income if presented).
Do not present or describe any items of income or expense as 'extraordinary items' in the statement of comprehensive income, income statement (if presented), or in the notes.

Present changes in equity for the reporting period, either in a statement of changes in equity or (if specified conditions are met and the entity chooses) in a statement of income and retained earnings.

Present in the statement of changes in equity: (a) profit or loss for the period; (b) other comprehensive income for the period; (c) effects of changes in accounting policies and corrections of material errors recognised in the period; (d) investments by equity investors during the period; (e) dividends and other distributions to equity investors during the period.
Present a statement of changes in equity showing the items required by paragraph 6.3

Classify interest paid as either an operating cash flow or a financing cash flow; classify interest received and dividends received as either operating cash flows or investing cash flows. No other classification is permitted for these items.

Do not exclude a subsidiary from consolidation on the grounds that its business activities are dissimilar to those of other entities within the group; where such dissimilar subsidiaries are consolidated, disclose additional information in the consolidated financial statements about their different business activities.
Present non-controlling interest in the consolidated statement of financial position within equity, separately from the equity of the owners of the parent.
Disclose non-controlling interest in the profit or loss of the group separately in the statement of comprehensive income (or income statement, if presented).

Attribute profit or loss, each component of other comprehensive income, and total comprehensive income to owners of the parent and to non-controlling interest separately, even if this results in the non-controlling interest having a deficit balance
Disclose the grounds on which the parent is exempt from presenting consolidated financial statements.

When a parent accounts for investments in subsidiaries, associates or jointly controlled entities at fair value through profit or loss in its individual financial statements, disclose the information required by Section 11 in respect of those investments (to comply with paragraph 36(4) of Schedule 1 to the Regulations).

Disclose in significant accounting policies (a) the measurement basis (or bases) used for financial instruments and (b) the other accounting policies used for financial instruments that are relevant to an understanding of the financial statements.
Where the entity uses hedge accounting under Section 12, make the additional disclosures required by paragraphs 12.27 to 12.29A.
Disclose summarised financial information about associates (including total assets, total liabilities, revenues and profit or loss) unless the entity uses the cost or fair value model
Disclose separately the investor's share of any discontinued operations of associates accounted for using the equity method.

Disclose for each class of property, plant and equipment: (a) the gross carrying amount and the accumulated depreciation (aggregated with accumulated impairment losses) at the beginning and end of the period; and (b) a reconciliation of the carrying amount at the beginning and end of the period showing additions, disposals, acquisitions through business combinations, revaluations, impairment losses recognised or reversed, depreciation, and other changes (paragraphs 17.31(d)–(e)).

Include a statement on the face of the statement of financial position, in a prominent position above the signature, that the financial statements are prepared in accordance with the provisions applicable to companies subject to the small companies regime.

Where the entity has invoked the serious-prejudice exemption under paragraph 21.17 and omitted some or all of the disclosures otherwise required by paragraphs 21.14–21.16, it shall disclose at minimum the items set out in the sub-paragraphs of 21.17 (being the minimum disclosures prescribed by those sub-paragraphs, which 21.17 itself introduces but does not enumerate).

requirement_text: Disclose the gross amount due to customers for contract work (a liability) as the net amount of costs incurred plus recognised profits less the sum of recognised losses and progress billings, for all contracts in progress for which progress billings exceed costs incurred plus recognised profits less recognised losses
When the presentation currency differs from the functional currency, state that fact, disclose the functional currency, and explain the reason for using a different presentation currency.
Disclose the date the financial statements were authorised for issue and who gave that authorisation.
Disclose key management personnel compensation in total.

Where the fair value of a biological asset previously measured at cost under paragraph 34.6A becomes reliably measurable during the current period, disclose why fair value has become reliably measurable and the effect of the change.
The financial statements of a retirement benefit plan shall distinguish between defined benefit and defined contribution elements, where material.

Present a statement of changes in net assets available for benefits (containing the specific items required by paragraph 34.37) within the financial statements of a retirement benefit plan, whether defined contribution or defined benefit

The financial statements of a retirement benefit plan (whether defined contribution or defined benefit) shall present the prescribed items in a statement of net assets available for benefits; the specific line items to be presented are set out in the sub-paragraphs of 34.38 and must be covered by subsequent checklist rows.

Commitments relating to heritage assets may be disclosed in aggregate (provided such aggregation does not obscure significant information), but recognised commitments and unrecognised commitments must be disclosed separately from each other.
